Earlier this year, there were rumors that iOS 26.4 would introduce a revamped Health app. That initiative was subsequently delayed, and after the release of iOS 27, this redesign was nowhere to be seen either.

With the next-generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to debut next month, it's worth asking: will these new features arrive alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's worth explaining why these features will most likely launch in September. You might be thinking, "Shouldn't all software be announced in June?" But in fact, there is genuine precedent for this kind of thing.

The Low Power Mode in watchOS 9, the sleep apnea detection feature in watchOS 11, and the hypertension notifications in watchOS 26 were all announced in September, even though they did not functionally depend on the latest hardware.

For these reasons, even though the latest Health app upgrade may not require a brand-new Apple Watch, Apple is still very likely to choose to wait until September for its official announcement.

There's Still Time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman had warned that the new Health app upgrade (codenamed Project Mulberry) might not appear in the WWDC keynote. That prediction turned out to be accurate:

Does this mean Project Mulberry is guaranteed to appear at the September event? Not necessarily. However, given the multiple precedents of brand-new features being announced in September, combined with the fact that we already knew it might arrive a little later than WWDC, the likelihood of a September debut remains quite high—even if it ultimately has to wait until October, arriving alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

Rumors about these features have been constantly evolving, because there are too many variables involved. You may have heard that one of the ideas was to launch a standalone Health+ service, complete with videos narrated by doctors. However, according to reports, those plans have been scaled back, and these features will ultimately be integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two things are already quite clear: first, an AI health coach will be added, providing recommendations based on your Health app data; second, the camera will be used to offer real-time guidance for fitness and other health-related activities. Another key part of this upgrade is a brand-new design for the Health app, making it easier for you to understand all the data.

Beyond that, we can only wait and see. Personally, I'm really looking forward to a better way to organize and understand my own Apple Health data.
